name: Cable Straight-Arm Pulldown
summary: A standing cable isolation exercise that targets the latissimus dorsi through shoulder extension with fixed, extended elbows.

setup: Attach a straight bar or wide handle to the high pulley of a cable station.
Grasp the bar with an overhand (pronated), shoulder-width grip.
Take a step or two back from the pulley, hinge slightly at the hips, and maintain a soft bend in the knees and a braced core.
Extend your arms overhead with a slight, fixed bend in the elbows.
steps: Drive your hands downward in a wide arc toward your upper thighs by contracting your lats.
Keep your elbow angle locked and fixed throughout the descent.
Squeeze your lats and depress your shoulder blades firmly at the bottom position near your thighs.
Control the weight back up along the same arc until you feel a deep stretch in your lats before initiating the next rep.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as your arms rise into the stretch; exhale as you pull the bar down toward your thighs.
cues: Sweep the bar down in a wide arc
Keep the elbows soft but locked
Crush oranges in your armpits at the bottom

common_faults.fault: Bending and extending the elbows during the movement, turning it into a triceps pushdown.
common_faults.correction: Lock a slight bend in your elbows at the setup and do not change elbow angle as the arms sweep.

common_faults.fault: Excessive torso swinging or momentum to drive the bar down.
common_faults.correction: Hinge slightly at the hips, brace your abdomen, and isolate the movement strictly to the shoulder joints.

precautions: Do not let the cable snap your arms overhead into extreme shoulder elevation if you lack mobility.
